turns.assessment: The simultaneous ~5 dB reductions in received power and estimated OSNR are confined to och85 at S12. Stable upstream OCM and amplifier telemetry strongly exclude span loss or amplifier faults, while unchanged BER and absence of a unit alarm argue against a hard line-interface failure. A channel-specific attenuation drift in the S12 receive/add-drop WSS, downstream of the line-side OCM, best fits the evidence.

proposals.rationale: A receive-side WSS attenuation increase at S12 can reduce only och85's power before trx.och85.z while remaining invisible to the line-side OCM. The soft 5 dB change and lack of signal-loss alarm match this mode.
proposals.note: site named; resolved to its node equipment

proposals.rationale: A receiver-local defect could produce anomalous local power and OSNR reporting while all upstream instruments remain stable, but documented RX degradation normally causes a receiver penalty or errors, and pre-FEC BER did not change.

clarify.assessment: och85 runs from trx.och85.a at S04 through S04–S20–S01–S12 to trx.och85.z. Therefore its receive-side WSS at S12 is on the S01-to-S12 ingress, identifying oms.S01-S12|15; the S15-to-S12 alternatives are not on och85's arriving path.
